history.summary: PROVISIONAL RECORD: the CSV spells this row 'ISCKON Temple' - that is a typo of ISKCON (International Society for Krishna Consciousness). No ISKCON-affiliated temple in Churachandpur is documented in any source found, and no ISKCON affiliation could be verified for any Churachandpur shrine. The well-known ISKCON centre in Manipur is ISKCON Imphal (Sri Sri Radha Krishnacandra) at Sangaiprou, Airport Road, Imphal - founded by Srila Bhaktisvarupa Damodara Swami, dome-shaped architecture, major Janmashtami and Ratha Yatra celebrations, about 60 km from Churachandpur - which the CSV row does NOT describe (CSV town is Churachandpur). The best-supported local candidate is the Shree Radha Krishna Mandir at Lighthouse Lane, Jangnomphai, Churachandpur 795128 (listed in the onefivenine Lamka Hindu-temples directory, ~2.9 km from central Lamka); Radha-Krishna temple listings for Churachandpur on vimarsana describe a Janmashtami-celebrating Krishna temple at Buribazar but one misplaces it in Bishnupur district. Whether the intended record is this local Radha-Krishna mandir or a small unlisted ISKCON preaching centre could not be confirmed; the ISKCON affiliation is unverified. Do not invent a location or founding date - verify on the ground before use. No reliable image found (media empty).

town_description: Churachandpur (locally called Lamka) is the second-largest town of Manipur and the headquarters of Churachandpur district, about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road. It is the heartland of the Kuki-Chin hill tribes (Thadou-Kuki, Hmar, Paite, Zou) and is overwhelmingly Christian; a small Hindu/Meitei community maintains a handful of shrines in and around the town, including the Shree Radha Krishna Mandir at Jangnomphai.

travel.airport: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport (Imphal, IMF) - about 60 km northeast of Churachandpur (verify).
travel.railway: No rail link to Churachandpur; nearest railhead is Dimapur (Nagaland) or Jiribam (verify).
travel.road: Churachandpur is about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road (NH-102B), connected by buses and shared sumos (verify schedules). The Jangnomphai Radha Krishna Mandir is a short drive from central Lamka (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami (Aug-Sep) is the major festival at Krishna temples.
